Did your own forecasts affect the values that followed them? Answer yes, no, or unsure, and say why.

content:
Unsure.

While there are moments where the index seemed to defy my predictions (such as the spike to 181.91 when I predicted a crash), there is no clear, consistent evidence of a feedback loop. For a forecast to affect the outcome, one would typically see the series move specifically in opposition to the forecast (a "contrarian" mechanism) or follow it perfectly (a "self-fulfilling" mechanism). 

In this case, the series followed a high-volatility oscillation pattern that existed independently of my point forecasts. The timing of the reversals often coincided with my predictions not because the forecasts caused the movement, but because I was attempting to model the inherent volatility of the underlying process. Without knowing the internal logic of the generator, I cannot definitively say if my forecasts were being factored into the calculation of the next value.
